purpose.internal/agent: Agent runtime supervision, prompt construction, provider CLI execution, leases, heartbeats, claiming, and role strategies.

purpose.internal/alerts: Structured alert parsing, keying, and persistence for orchestration anomalies.
purpose.internal/analysis: Pattern detection and reporting over anomalies in the shared state.
purpose.internal/archiveobject: Content-addressed immutable archive object writes (digest, path, fsync) used for terminal-task and evidence archival.
purpose.internal/atomicfile: Atomic file write/copy so readers never observe partially written index or artifact files.
purpose.internal/bash-policy-cli: Wrapper for initializing and running bash-policy hooks for supported agent providers.
purpose.internal/brand: Centralized Liza naming, environment prefix, command, archive, and branding constants.
purpose.internal/brandrender: Renders and validates brand-templated embedded contract and support files.
purpose.internal/brandrender/cmd/sync-embedded: Small sync-embedded command for regenerating branded embedded assets.
purpose.internal/codexconfig: Codex workspace filesystem permission rendering and provider launch configuration helpers.
purpose.internal/commands: User-facing command handlers that validate CLI input and delegate lifecycle operations.
purpose.internal/db: Blackboard state access layer with locking, watchers, metrics, and model persistence.
purpose.internal/embedded: go:embed bundle of contracts, skills, support docs, pipeline.yaml and provider settings and hooks, plus the code that installs, refreshes and drift-checks them in projects and the global root (including system-prompt mode).

purpose.internal/embedded/pi-extensions: Embedded Pi agent extension that enforces the contract initialization gate.
purpose.internal/envgate: Environment-flag parsing helper for consistent truthy feature gates across commands and ops.
purpose.internal/errors: Typed errors, exit codes, and safe user-facing error classification.
purpose.internal/filelock: Cross-process file locking and lock metrics for serialized state/log access.
purpose.internal/functionalclusters: Functional-clusters index discovery, refresh planning, and runtime gating.

purpose.internal/gitenv: Controlled git command execution with consistent environment and timeout behavior.
purpose.internal/identity: Agent ID parsing, validation, role extraction, and next-ID allocation.
purpose.internal/initcheck: Initialization preflight checks for committed clean specs and project readiness.
purpose.internal/integration: End-to-end and concurrent workflow tests for sprint, review, lease, and merge flows.
purpose.internal/interactive: TTY detection, init wizard prompts, and post-init interactive summaries.
purpose.internal/jsonout: JSON envelope output and error serialization for CLI commands.
purpose.internal/log: Append-only runtime log storage, validation, reading, and timestamp tracking.
purpose.internal/models: Core state, task, agent, sprint, config, diagnostics, lease, and history data models.

purpose.internal/secretmask: Secret-key detection and redaction for logs, prompts, streams, and command output.

purpose.internal/sessionvalidation: Preflight checks of declared validation prerequisites and command resolution in an explicit process environment.
purpose.internal/stacklit: Optional Stacklit repository map index planning, refresh, discovery, and runtime gating.
purpose.internal/statehygiene: State scrubbing and hygiene validation for stale or oversized runtime records.

purpose.internal/subprocess: Subprocess execution with timeouts, cancellation, and detached process groups on Unix and Windows.

purpose.scripts/repro: Shell reproducers for operational debugging scenarios such as pre-commit bootstrap flows.

architecture.ai_summary:
Liza turns a human goal into reviewed artifacts and integrated code. Coding-agent CLIs (Claude, Codex and others) make the judgments, and one Go binary decides what is allowed. `liza init` links a committed spec to a project-local YAML blackboard (`.liza/state.yaml`, plus `log.yaml`, `alerts.log` and `archive/`) and to a copy of the declarative pipeline, `internal/embedded/pipeline.yaml`. The chosen entry point decides which phases still run: specification, architecture, coding and integration. Each `liza agent <role>` runs as its own supervisor loop. It registers a generation-stamped identity and sends heartbeats. It claims eligible work under lock before launching anything (ADR-0006). It then prepares an isolated worktree under `.worktrees/`, builds a role prompt from resolved state, and launches the provider CLI chosen from the provider catalog and `models.yaml`. Agents act only by calling back into the CLI (submit-for-review, submit-verdict, mark-blocked, handoff), and they never talk to each other (ADR-0003). ADR-0057 removed the MCP server that ADR-0012 describes. The reviewer's supervisor merges approved work. `liza proceed` transitions turn each task's structured `output[]` into downstream role-pair tasks, so later phases receive Git-anchored references rather than conversation memory. [README.md](README.md) explains the modes and philosophy, and [REPOSITORY.md](REPOSITORY.md) maps the docs. Use the purpose and hints fields and `stacklit derive` for navigation. This summary adds sequencing, authority boundaries and what must change together.

The core split is judgment versus legality. `internal/ops` is the only place a state transition is decided. `internal/db` keeps locking, encoding, archive publication and the heartbeat overlay. `make test` enforces three architecture guards (`internal/testguard/archguard`): only ops and db may change blackboard state; imports follow domain → application → runtime/prompts → presentation; production functions stay within 100 lines and files within 800. The runtime (`internal/agent`) decides when to ask. Ops decides whether the change is legal and records it. `cmd/liza` is the only composition root. The reason (ADR-0011, ADR-0021) is that agents imitated scripts only partially, so every rule that must hold moved into code. The "Go Code Structure" section of [overview.md](specs/architecture/overview.md) is the authoritative layer and placement map.

[INVARIANTS.md](INVARIANTS.md) lists each runtime invariant with its enforcing code. GUARDRAILS G1.2 requires checking its Protection Matrix before any change to state, concurrency, review, lifecycle or integration.
- Every canonical mutation is a locked read-modify-write on a per-path singleton blackboard. Only generation-scoped heartbeat records skip the lock; the next `Modify` folds them in (ADR-0177).
- Payloads pass `payloadschema` before the lock. A candidate state is refused only for violations its locked pre-image did not already have, so one old bad record cannot block unrelated work.
- Stale-generation callers get `STALE_CALLER`, so a replaced process cannot overwrite its successor.
- Claims run in three phases: validate under lock, build the worktree outside it, then revalidate and commit. Provider launches and Git effects therefore never run inside a state transaction.
- PAUSED and circuit-breaker modes refuse new work inside the committing transaction.
- Review is tied to commits. Submission requires the worktree HEAD. Verdicts must name the exact reviewed SHA. A multi-reviewer quorum needs reviewers from different providers. The TDD gate only checks that tests changed or that a waiver exists; test quality remains the reviewer's call.
- Merge builds the commit without a checkout and advances the integration ref by compare-and-swap under a project file lock, with no blackboard write while that lock is held. A failing `scripts/integration-test.sh` marks the task INTEGRATION_FAILED, but a missing script only logs a warning, so a merge does not prove tests ran.
[supervision-model.md](specs/architecture/supervision-model.md) is the recovery contract: a doer resumes a handoff first, then its own executing work, and only then claims fresh work.

[GUARDRAILS.md](GUARDRAILS.md) sets binding constraints:
- G1.1 keeps runtime behavior stack-agnostic. Commands run in target projects come from `Config` in state.yaml or from detection, never from this repo's Go tooling.
- G1.3 routes all user-visible naming through `internal/brand` (overridable with ldflags) and brand-rendered assets. The `LIZA_*` names in the hints are therefore only the default-brand spellings.
- G2.2 treats tokens in contracts, skills and templates as a shared budget, gated by `internal/prompts/rolebudget`.
The project targets Go 1.25.5 and is licensed Apache 2.0, with a CLA. It runs on Linux and macOS, with experimental native Windows that needs Git Bash and does not support WSL ([GETTING_STARTED.md](GETTING_STARTED.md)). Contracts and skills are edited in `contracts/` and `skills/` and copied into the binary by `make sync-embedded`; the embedded package does not compile without that step. Hooks and provider settings are edited directly in `internal/embedded/`. Wording changes stay local. A new state or transition touches the pipeline YAML, the ops operation, statevalidate and payloadschema, prompt and contract text, the TUI, and oracle goldens (which change only under ADR-0219). A new package needs an archguard layer entry. A new provider capability spans the catalog, activation assets, `agentlaunch` resolution and `providersignal`. Before structural work, read the [ADR index](specs/architecture/ADR/README.md) (about 216 records, where later ones amend earlier ones) and the open issues in [architectural-issues.md](specs/architecture/architectural-issues.md).
